The FOMC decided to maintain interest rates at the 3.75%-4.00% rate on Wednesday, as widely expected by investors, citing economic activity expanding at a strong pace. Two dissents were served by Fed Gov. Lisa Cook and Cleaveland Fed President Beth Hammack.
In addition, the focus will be on Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s press conference for signals on the policy outlook and the possibility of future rate hikes.

“The Fed is underestimating what it will take to restore price stability under current conditions, as the energy shock that the central bank originally would fade is intensifying,” said Joseph Brusuelas, RSM US principal and chief economist.

“We expect that the Fed will hike at every other meeting until there are obvious signs that inflation is abating, financial conditions are tightening, and/or the economy slows back below its long-term 2% trend,” Brusuelas added.
